receipts.description: One entry per physical receipt in reading order. Never merge, skip or deduplicate look-alike receipts.

date.description: Transaction date as DD-MM-YYYY (e.g. 26-05-2026), day first as the receipt prints it, no time. Null if the day, month or year is unreadable.

discount.description: Positive total discount or subsidy actually applied to this transaction, in rupiah. 0 if none or not proven by the transaction lines.

total.description: Final amount paid for the whole receipt. Not cash tendered, change or tax.

quantity.description: Volume in liters; the separator is a decimal point.

unit_price.description: GROSS rupiah per liter before any discount or subsidy, never the reduced price. Null if unsupported.

total_price.description: GROSS product amount before discount, not the amount paid when a discount exists. Null if unsupported.

confidence.description: How sure you are that each value of this product is exactly what is printed, as a number from 0.0 to 1.0. Judge only how readable the characters are and how clear their meaning is, never because the arithmetic fits. 0.95 to 1.0: every character is sharp and the meaning is clear. 0.80 to 0.94: one character is faint or could be mistaken for another. 0.50 to 0.79: you are choosing between two or more readings. Below 0.50: mostly a guess. 0.0: the value is null. Do not give 0.99 unless you checked every character.

name.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Is every letter and digit of the name exactly as printed (BP92 and EP92 are different names)? Lower it when a character could be another one (B/E, 0/O, 5/S, 1/I, 8/B).

quantity.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Is every digit and the decimal point of the liters exactly as printed? Lower it when a digit is faint or the comma/point could be read either way.

unit_price.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Is every digit and separator right, and is it the gross price per liter? Lower it when you cannot tell whether the printed price is gross or already reduced.

total_price.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Is every digit and separator right, and is it the gross product amount? Lower it when it could be the amount paid after a discount, or when a digit is faint.

confidence.description: How sure you are that each value of this receipt is exactly what is printed, as a number from 0.0 to 1.0. Judge only how readable the characters are and how clear their meaning is, never because the arithmetic fits. 0.95 to 1.0: every character is sharp and the meaning is clear. 0.80 to 0.94: one character is faint or could be mistaken for another. 0.50 to 0.79: you are choosing between two or more readings. Below 0.50: mostly a guess. 0.0: the value is null. Do not give 0.99 unless you checked every character.

date.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Is every digit (or month name) of the day, month and year read exactly as printed? Lower it whenever any digit could be another one (3/8, 5/6, 6/8, 1/7, 0/8, 2/7), even if the date looks reasonable. 0.0 if the date is null.

discount.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Confidence in the discount amount, or in 'no discount' when it is 0. Lower it when two prices differ but no line labels the difference as a discount or subsidy.

total.description: 0.0 to 1.0. Is every digit and separator of the final amount paid right? Lower it when a digit is faint or when Total, cash tendered (Tunai) and change (Kembali) could be mixed up.
